walkthrough:
Substitute the known exact trigonometric value $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ into the equation:
$$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \tan(2x) + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 0$$
$$\sqrt{3} + \tan(2x) = 0 \implies \tan(2x) = -\sqrt{3}$$

Determine the corresponding interval for $2x$:
$$-\frac{\pi}{4} < x < \frac{\pi}{4} \implies -\frac{\pi}{2} < 2x < \frac{\pi}{2}$$

Divide by 2 to find the exact value of $x$:
$$x = -\frac{\pi}{6}$$
